title: Private Deployments VPC & On-Prem Reference: Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, Customer Requirements Library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates our reference guidance for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem packaging) with an emphasis on day-2 operations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library to accelerate scoping and successful deployments. It is intended for solutions engineers, platform operators, and SREs supporting private customers.

Scope

- VPC-deployed private control plane and on-prem inference clusters
- Packaging formats (OCI images, installers, Helm charts) and recommended artifact signing
- Day-2 operational practices: monitoring, backups, capacity adjustments, scaling, and incident handling
- Upgrade and rollback playbooks for control plane and runtime components
- Customer requirements library (network, IAM, storage, compliance checklist)

Reference architecture summary

1) VPC-deployed Private Control Plane (recommended for most enterprise customers)
- Control plane components: api-gateway, auth-service, config-store, orchestration, policy-engine, metrics-collector.
- Data plane (customer-managed): inference clusters (K8s or bare metal), object store (S3 or S3-compatible), KMS integration for keys.
- Network boundaries: dedicated VPC, private subnets for control plane, peered/transit VPC for data-plane access, optional AWS PrivateLink for management plane.

2) On-prem Inference Clusters
- Packaging: signed OCI images + Helm chart for air-gapped environments; optional installer (tarball) with SHA256 checksums and GPG signatures.
- Deployment mode: Kubernetes (>=1.26) recommended for orchestration; validated bare-metal pack for environments without K8s.
- Storage: local NVMe for model KV cache + NFS/SMB for persistent logs and backups (encrypted at rest).

Minimum hardware profile (single-node inference)

| Component            | Minimum (dev/test)        | Recommended (prod)         | Notes |
|---------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------|-------|
| GPU                 | 1 x A10 / T4              | 4 x A100 / H100 per node   | Model-size dependent |
| RAM                 | 64 GB                     | 512 GB                     | KV cache + batching needs |
| Local storage       | 1 TB NVMe                 | 4 TB NVMe                  | models + cache |
| Network             | 1 Gbps                    | 10 Gbps                    | low-latency between nodes |

(Use this table as a baseline; adjust for customer model suites and SLOs.)

Packaging and artifact guidance

- Artifact formats: OCI images (primary), Helm charts (v3), signed tarball installers for air-gapped installs.
- Signing & provenance: all images must be signed with in-house image-signing key (Cosign) and have SBOMs (CycloneDX).
- Versioning: semver for all releases; control-plane and runtime versions must be declared separately in release notes and the release matrix.
- Air-gap packaging: provide an offline bundle script that produces an installer.tar.gz with images, Helm charts, CRDs, and a bootstrap manifest.

VPC deployment checklist (pre-deploy)

1. Networking
   - Allocate dedicated VPC and subnets (private for control plane).
   - Reserve CIDR blocks (avoid overlaps with customer on-prem CIDRs if peering/VPN required).
   - Configure security groups, NACLs with least privilege (list of required ports below).
2. Identity & Access
   - Establish SSO/OIDC config (SCIM provisioning optional).
   - Provide service principal with scoped permissions for cloud resources (S3 read/write, KMS encrypt/decrypt).
3. Secrets & Keys
   - Integrate with customer KMS or HSM for envelope encryption; require rotated keys and access audits.
4. Observability
   - Configure metrics ingest endpoint (Prometheus remote_write or hosted ingest) and log forwarder (Fluentd/Fluent Bit).

Required network ports (example)

- 443 TCP: control plane API endpoints (HTTPS)
- 22 TCP: (optional) admin access - use bastion only
- 9090 TCP: Prometheus metrics endpoint (internal)
- 50051 TCP: gRPC control-plane internal (between control and data plane)
- NFS/SMB ports: for shared storage where applicable

Day-2 operations (operational playbook)

Ownership and runbooks
- Owner: private-deployments team (+ oncall rotation from eng-sre).
- Runbooks: start/stop components, scale inference nodes, replace failed GPU node, rotate keys, investigate latency regressions.

Common day-2 tasks (procedures)

1) Scale inference cluster (Kubernetes):
   a. Check current utilization: kubectl -n inference top nodes / pods
   b. Update machine pool/VMSS ASG capacity or adjust cluster-autoscaler configuration
   c. Observe rolling additions in metrics dashboard (CPU/GPU utilisation, queue length)

2) Replace failed node (bare-metal):
   1. Move workloads off node: cordon and drain (k8s) or stop runtime (bare-metal).
   2. Replace hardware or reprovision VM image with approved OS and packages.
   3. Rejoin node to cluster and validate model warming and KV cache priming.

3) Backups & restores:
   - Configuration: daily control-plane config export to encrypted S3 bucket with 30-day retention.
   - Procedure: restore config -> restart control plane -> reconcile runtime nodes. Test restore monthly in staging.

Monitoring & alerting recommendations

- SLOs: 95th latency target per route (configurable per customer); error budget tracking in SLO dashboard.
- Key alerts: model-serving error rate >1% (5m), control-plane API 5xx rate >0.5% (5m), KV cache miss rate spike, GPU OOMs, disk pressure >80%.
- Dashboards: per-customer per-model latency, tokens/sec, batching efficiency, model cache hit-rate, GPU temperature and power.

Upgrade and rollback procedures

Principles
- Prefer canary first: deploy new control-plane version to a small percentage of customers (or a dedicated canary cluster).
- Maintain backward compatibility for API surface where feasible.
- Keep a tested rollback manifest for every release.

Control-plane upgrade (high-level steps)

1. Preflight: run smoke tests, validate schema compatibility, ensure DB migrations are reversible.
2. Canary: deploy to canary cluster (or 1 control-plane instance) and run synthetic traffic load for 24-72 hours.
3. Gradual rollout: incrementally increase traffic percentage and monitor SLOs and key logs.
4. Full rollout: roll through all regions/clusters if metrics stable.
5. Post-mortem: capture any anomalies and update release notes.

Rollback checklist (if anomalies detected)

- Trigger conditions: sustained SLO violations for >15 minutes or critical error spikes.
- Steps: pause rollout, revert control-plane manifest to previous version, redeploy old image(s), re-run smoke tests, reopen traffic.
- Communication: notify stakeholders (oncall, support, customer success) and create incident ticket.

Runtime (inference) upgrade considerations

- Model runtime upgrades (e.g., kernel changes, quantization support) require validation across representative model shapes.
- Warmup strategy: pre-load KV cache for large models to avoid latency spikes.
- Rolling restart: drain node of new sessions before kernel updates; use workload-aware batching during transitions.

Customer requirements library (scoping checklist)

Use the following checklist during pre-sales and onboarding to capture customer environment constraints and compliance needs. Capture answers as part of the onboarding ticket.

1) Networking
   - Does customer require private connectivity (VPN/Direct Connect/ExpressRoute)?
   - Are there CIDR conflicts with existing networks?
   - Are NAT gateways or egress proxies required?
2) Identity & Auth
   - Preferred identity provider (Okta/AzureAD/OneLogin)?
   - SCIM provisioning required?
   - KMS/HSM provider and access policies?
3) Data residency & compliance
   - Required regions for data residency?
   - Log retention policy, audit logging requirements, SOC2/GDPR/HIPAA constraints?
4) Hardware constraints
   - Allowed GPU types, rack space, power limits, cooling constraints for on-prem installs?
5) Operational constraints
   - Maintenance windows, patching SLA, backup retention SLAs, support escalation paths?

Template: customer requirements answer fields
- customer_name
- deployment_mode (vpc/on-prem)
- primary_region_or_datacenter
- connectivity_mode (vpn/direct-connect/private-link)
- identity_provider
- kms_provider
- required_slos (p95 latency, availability)
- retention_and_audit_reqs
- hardware_constraints
- allowed_third_party_endpoints

Ownership, support & escalation

- Primary owners: private-deployments (implementation) and eng-sre (operational oncall).
- Escalation path: private-deployments -> eng-sre -> platform -> engineering leadership.
- Support SLAs: refer to customer contract; ensure playbooks aligned with response/resolve timelines.

Appendices

A. Example CLI snippets
- Generate offline bundle: ./packaging/build-offline-bundle.sh --version 2029.01.10 --output ./bundle.tar.gz
- Validate image signature: cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.company/repo:tag

B. Common troubleshooting checklist
1) High p95 latency: check KV cache hit-rate -> priming job -> increase pre-warm replicas.
2) Increased 5xx errors: inspect control-plane logs, check DB connectivity and migration state.
3) GPU OOMs: reduce per-request max length, enable early batching fallbacks, or upgrade node type.

C. Related pages
- Private deployments operational guide (runbooks) - see related pages above.
- Packaging & image release policy - internal link in release-mgmt.

Document maintenance

- Owner: Aisha Patel (private-deployments).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after each major release.
- Last reviewed: 2029-01-15.

For questions or to request a new template for a customer, open a ticket in the private-deployments board and tag @private-deployments.
